req.title: Login sets session on success
req.statement: The system shall set session['user_id'] and redirect to / when POST /auth/login receives a matching username and password.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-008 requires that POST /auth/login with valid credentials returns HTTP 302 redirecting to '/' and sets session['user_id']. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — valid username+password yields 302 to '/' with session cookie set; (2) negative NEG — wrong password yields no redirect and no session; (3) negative NEG — unknown username yields no redirect; (4) BVA/STC — session is cleared before setting user_id (state transition: logged-in user logs in again gets fresh session); (5) DT — all four combinations of username/password correctness. Assertions use exact status codes (302 not >=300), exact Location header value ('/' not any string), and session inspection via app.test_request_context to confirm user_id is set to the exact integer id from the preloaded fixture.

tests.name: test_login_valid_credentials_redirects_to_index_and_sets_session
expected: Session cookie is present in response
Subsequent request with same client shows g.user loaded (session['user_id']==1)
trace: R-FLASKR-008: session['user_id'] set and redirect to / on success
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
with client:
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/', f'Expected Location="/", got {r.headers["Location"]}'
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert 'user_id' in sess, 'session["user_id"] not set after successful login'
        assert sess['user_id'] == 1, f'Expected user_id=1, got {sess["user_id"]}'
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_login_clears_previous_session_and_sets_new_user_id
preconditions: Client already has a session with user_id=2 (Anjali)
actions: Manually set session['user_id']=2 to simulate prior login
expected: Exactly one key 'user_id' in session (session.clear() was called)
trace: R-FLASKR-008: session.clear() then session['user_id']=user['id'] — state transition from logged-in-as-other to logged-in-as-new
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
with client:
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        sess['user_id'] = 2
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/', f'Expected Location="/", got {r.headers["Location"]}'
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert sess.get('user_id') == 1, f'Expected user_id=1 after re-login, got {sess.get("user_id")}'
        assert sess.get('user_id') != 2, 'Old session user_id=2 must be cleared'
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_login_all_preloaded_users_valid_credentials
preconditions: All 5 users exist with known plain-text passwords
actions: POST /auth/login for each of the 5 preloaded users with correct credentials
expected: Each login sets session['user_id'] to the correct integer id
trace: R-FLASKR-008: decision table — all valid (username, password) pairs must succeed
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

users = [(1,'Rahul','stone'),(2,'Anjali','cloud'),(3,'Ishaan','stone'),(4,'Diya','cloud'),(5,'James','river')]
for uid, uname, pwd in users:
    client = app.test_client()
    with client:
        r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': uname, 'password': pwd})
        assert r.status_code == 302, f'User {uname}: expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.headers['Location'] == '/', f'User {uname}: expected Location="/", got {r.headers["Location"]}'
        with client.session_transaction() as sess:
            assert sess.get('user_id') == uid, f'User {uname}: expected user_id={uid}, got {sess.get("user_id")}'
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_login_correct_username_wrong_password_boundary_check
actions: POST /auth/login with username='James' and password='river' (correct) — expect 302
POST /auth/login with username='James' and password='River' (wrong case) — expect 200 with error
expected: Wrong-case password: 200, 'Incorrect password.' in body, no session user_id
trace: R-FLASKR-008: BVA on password matching — one character difference (case) must not authenticate; catches == vs is / hash comparison mutations
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
with client:
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'James', 'password': 'river'})
    assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert sess.get('user_id') == 5

client2 = app.test_client()
with client2:
    r2 = client2.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'James', 'password': 'River'})
    assert r2.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 for wrong-case password, got {r2.status_code}'
    assert b'Incorrect password.' in r2.data
    with client2.session_transaction() as sess2:
        assert 'user_id' not in sess2
os.unlink(path)
